summary.fr: Un pauvre colporteur fait trois fois le même rêve : un trésor l’attend sur le pont de Londres. Il décide de partir.
summary.en: A poor pedlar has the same dream three times: a treasure awaits him on London Bridge. He decides to set off.

paragraphs.jp: Long ago, in the little town of Swaffham, there lived a poor pedlar called John Chapman.
paragraphs.fr: Il y a longtemps, dans la petite ville de Swaffham, vivait un pauvre colporteur nommé John Chapman.
paragraphs.en: Long ago, in the little town of Swaffham, there lived a poor pedlar called John Chapman.
paragraphs.kana: Long ago, in the little town of Swaffham, there lived a poor pedlar called John Chapman.

paragraphs.jp: One night he dreamt that if he went to London Bridge, he would hear some wonderful news.
paragraphs.fr: Une nuit, il rêva que s’il allait au pont de Londres, il apprendrait une merveilleuse nouvelle.
paragraphs.en: One night he dreamt that if he went to London Bridge, he would hear some wonderful news.
paragraphs.kana: One night he dreamt that if he went to London Bridge, he would hear some wonderful news.

paragraphs.jp: He had the same dream three nights in a row, so he decided to go.
paragraphs.fr: Il fit le même rêve trois nuits de suite ; il décida donc de partir.
paragraphs.en: He had the same dream three nights in a row, so he decided to go.
paragraphs.kana: He had the same dream three nights in a row, so he decided to go.

paragraphs.jp: His wife thought he was mad. “It must be the cheese you ate before bed,” she said.
paragraphs.fr: Sa femme le crut fou. « Ça doit être le fromage que tu as mangé avant de te coucher », dit-elle.
paragraphs.en: His wife thought he was mad. “It must be the cheese you ate before bed,” she said.
paragraphs.kana: His wife thought he was mad. “It must be the cheese you ate before bed,” she said.

q.fr: Combien de fois John fait-il le rêve ?
q.en: How many times does John have the dream?
What does his wife think?

paragraphs.jp: John walked for days until he reached London Bridge. He waited there from morning till night, but nothing happened.
paragraphs.fr: John marcha des jours jusqu’au pont de Londres. Il y attendit du matin au soir, mais rien ne se passa.
paragraphs.en: John walked for days until he reached London Bridge. He waited there from morning till night, but nothing happened.
paragraphs.kana: John walked for days until he reached London Bridge. He waited there from morning till night, but nothing happened.

paragraphs.jp: On the third day, a shopkeeper asked him why he had been standing there for so long.
paragraphs.fr: Le troisième jour, un commerçant lui demanda pourquoi il restait planté là depuis si longtemps.
paragraphs.en: On the third day, a shopkeeper asked him why he had been standing there for so long.
paragraphs.kana: On the third day, a shopkeeper asked him why he had been standing there for so long.

paragraphs.jp: When John told him about his dream, the shopkeeper laughed. “I had a dream too,” he said.
paragraphs.fr: Quand John lui parla de son rêve, le commerçant éclata de rire. « Moi aussi, j’ai fait un rêve », dit-il.
paragraphs.en: When John told him about his dream, the shopkeeper laughed. “I had a dream too,” he said.
paragraphs.kana: When John told him about his dream, the shopkeeper laughed. “I had a dream too,” he said.

paragraphs.jp: “I dreamt that a treasure was buried under a tree in the garden of a pedlar in Swaffham. But I would never be so foolish as to go there!”
paragraphs.fr: « J’ai rêvé qu’un trésor était enterré sous un arbre, dans le jardin d’un colporteur de Swaffham. Mais je ne serais jamais assez sot pour y aller ! »
paragraphs.en: “I dreamt that a treasure was buried under a tree in the garden of a pedlar in Swaffham. But I would never be so foolish as to go there!”
paragraphs.kana: “I dreamt that a treasure was buried under a tree in the garden of a pedlar in Swaffham. But I would never be so foolish as to go there!”

q.fr: Que demande le commerçant à John ?
q.en: What does the shopkeeper ask John?

choices.fr: Pourquoi il attend là depuis si longtemps
choices.en: Why he has been waiting there so long
If he wants to buy something

q.fr: Où se trouve le trésor dans le rêve du commerçant ?
q.en: Where is the treasure in the shopkeeper’s dream?

choices.fr: Dans le jardin d’un colporteur de Swaffham

paragraphs.jp: John said nothing and hurried home. As soon as he arrived, he started digging under the old oak tree in his garden.
paragraphs.fr: John ne dit rien et rentra chez lui en hâte. Dès son arrivée, il se mit à creuser sous le vieux chêne de son jardin.
paragraphs.en: John said nothing and hurried home. As soon as he arrived, he started digging under the old oak tree in his garden.
paragraphs.kana: John said nothing and hurried home. As soon as he arrived, he started digging under the old oak tree in his garden.

paragraphs.jp: Soon his spade hit something hard: a pot full of gold coins.
paragraphs.fr: Bientôt, sa bêche heurta quelque chose de dur : une marmite pleine de pièces d’or.
paragraphs.en: Soon his spade hit something hard: a pot full of gold coins.
paragraphs.kana: Soon his spade hit something hard: a pot full of gold coins.

paragraphs.jp: John became a rich man, but he never forgot that he had once been poor.
paragraphs.fr: John devint riche, mais il n’oublia jamais qu’il avait été pauvre.
paragraphs.en: John became a rich man, but he never forgot that he had once been poor.
paragraphs.kana: John became a rich man, but he never forgot that he had once been poor.

paragraphs.jp: He used some of his gold to rebuild the church of Swaffham, where you can still see his statue today.
paragraphs.fr: Il utilisa une partie de son or pour reconstruire l’église de Swaffham, où l’on peut encore voir sa statue aujourd’hui.
paragraphs.en: He used some of his gold to rebuild the church of Swaffham, where you can still see his statue today.
paragraphs.kana: He used some of his gold to rebuild the church of Swaffham, where you can still see his statue today.

q.en: Where does John find the treasure?

choices.fr: Sous le chêne de son jardin
choices.en: Under the oak in his garden

q.fr: Que fait John avec une partie de son or ?
q.en: What does John do with some of his gold?

choices.en: He gives it to the shopkeeper

summary.fr: Dans la forêt de Carterhaugh, la jeune Janet rencontre Tam Lin, un chevalier prisonnier de la reine des fées. Pour le sauver, elle devra tenir bon une nuit entière.
summary.en: In the forest of Carterhaugh, young Janet meets Tam Lin, a knight held captive by the Queen of the Fairies. To save him, she will have to hold on for a whole night.

paragraphs.jp: Every young woman in the Scottish Borders had been warned never to go to Carterhaugh, a forest which was said to be guarded by an elf knight.
paragraphs.fr: Toutes les jeunes filles des Borders écossais avaient été averties de ne jamais aller à Carterhaugh, une forêt que l’on disait gardée par un chevalier elfe.
paragraphs.en: Every young woman in the Scottish Borders had been warned never to go to Carterhaugh, a forest which was said to be guarded by an elf knight.
paragraphs.kana: Every young woman in the Scottish Borders had been warned never to go to Carterhaugh, a forest which was said to be guarded by an elf knight.

paragraphs.jp: Janet, however, was not the kind of person who did what she was told.
paragraphs.fr: Janet, cependant, n’était pas du genre à obéir aux ordres.
paragraphs.en: Janet, however, was not the kind of person who did what she was told.
paragraphs.kana: Janet, however, was not the kind of person who did what she was told.

paragraphs.jp: She had barely picked a single rose when a young man appeared, asking her who had given her permission to be there.
paragraphs.fr: Elle avait à peine cueilli une rose qu’un jeune homme apparut et lui demanda qui lui avait permis d’être là.
paragraphs.en: She had barely picked a single rose when a young man appeared, asking her who had given her permission to be there.
paragraphs.kana: She had barely picked a single rose when a young man appeared, asking her who had given her permission to be there.

paragraphs.jp: “Carterhaugh is mine,” Janet replied. “My father gave it to me, so I need nobody’s permission.”
paragraphs.fr: « Carterhaugh m’appartient, répondit Janet. Mon père me l’a donnée, je n’ai donc besoin de la permission de personne. »
paragraphs.en: “Carterhaugh is mine,” Janet replied. “My father gave it to me, so I need nobody’s permission.”
paragraphs.kana: “Carterhaugh is mine,” Janet replied. “My father gave it to me, so I need nobody’s permission.”

q.fr: Que disait-on de la forêt de Carterhaugh ?
q.en: What was said about the forest of Carterhaugh?

choices.fr: Qu’elle était gardée par un chevalier elfe
choices.en: That it was guarded by an elf knight
That it was full of treasure

q.fr: Pourquoi Janet dit-elle n’avoir besoin d’aucune permission ?
q.en: Why does Janet say she needs no permission?

choices.fr: Son père lui a donné la forêt
choices.en: Her father gave her the forest

paragraphs.jp: The young man, whose name was Tam Lin, explained that he had once been a mortal knight.
paragraphs.fr: Le jeune homme, qui s’appelait Tam Lin, expliqua qu’il avait autrefois été un chevalier mortel.
paragraphs.en: The young man, whose name was Tam Lin, explained that he had once been a mortal knight.
paragraphs.kana: The young man, whose name was Tam Lin, explained that he had once been a mortal knight.

paragraphs.jp: Years before, he had fallen from his horse, and the Queen of the Fairies had caught him and taken him to her kingdom.
paragraphs.fr: Des années plus tôt, il était tombé de cheval, et la reine des fées l’avait rattrapé et emmené dans son royaume.
paragraphs.en: Years before, he had fallen from his horse, and the Queen of the Fairies had caught him and taken him to her kingdom.
paragraphs.kana: Years before, he had fallen from his horse, and the Queen of the Fairies had caught him and taken him to her kingdom.

paragraphs.jp: “Every seven years, the fairies pay a price to hell, and I fear I will be the price this time,” he said.
paragraphs.fr: « Tous les sept ans, les fées paient un tribut à l’enfer, et je crains d’être ce tribut cette fois-ci », dit-il.
paragraphs.en: “Every seven years, the fairies pay a price to hell, and I fear I will be the price this time,” he said.
paragraphs.kana: “Every seven years, the fairies pay a price to hell, and I fear I will be the price this time,” he said.

paragraphs.jp: “If you truly want to save me, you must pull me from my horse on Halloween night and hold me tight, whatever happens.”
paragraphs.fr: « Si tu veux vraiment me sauver, tu devras me faire tomber de cheval la nuit d’Halloween et me tenir serré, quoi qu’il arrive. »
paragraphs.en: “If you truly want to save me, you must pull me from my horse on Halloween night and hold me tight, whatever happens.”
paragraphs.kana: “If you truly want to save me, you must pull me from my horse on Halloween night and hold me tight, whatever happens.”

q.fr: Comment Tam Lin est-il devenu prisonnier des fées ?
q.en: How did Tam Lin become the fairies’ prisoner?

choices.fr: Il est tombé de cheval et la reine l’a emmené
choices.en: He fell from his horse and the Queen took him

choices.fr: Il est né chez les fées
choices.en: He was born among the fairies

q.fr: Que doit faire Janet la nuit d’Halloween ?
q.en: What must Janet do on Halloween night?

choices.fr: Le faire tomber de cheval et le tenir serré
choices.en: Pull him from his horse and hold him tight

paragraphs.jp: At midnight, the fairy procession rode past, and Janet recognised Tam Lin on a white horse. She pulled him down and held him in her arms.
paragraphs.fr: À minuit, le cortège des fées passa et Janet reconnut Tam Lin sur un cheval blanc. Elle le fit tomber et le serra dans ses bras.
paragraphs.en: At midnight, the fairy procession rode past, and Janet recognised Tam Lin on a white horse. She pulled him down and held him in her arms.
paragraphs.kana: At midnight, the fairy procession rode past, and Janet recognised Tam Lin on a white horse. She pulled him down and held him in her arms.

paragraphs.jp: Furious, the Queen turned him into a snake, then a lion, then a burning piece of iron, but Janet did not let go.
paragraphs.fr: Furieuse, la reine le transforma en serpent, puis en lion, puis en morceau de fer brûlant, mais Janet ne lâcha pas prise.
paragraphs.en: Furious, the Queen turned him into a snake, then a lion, then a burning piece of iron, but Janet did not let go.
paragraphs.kana: Furious, the Queen turned him into a snake, then a lion, then a burning piece of iron, but Janet did not let go.

paragraphs.jp: At last, Tam Lin became a man again. “Had I known what a human heart could do,” said the Queen bitterly, “I would have taken his eyes.”
paragraphs.fr: Enfin, Tam Lin redevint un homme. « Si j’avais su de quoi un cœur humain est capable, dit la reine avec amertume, je lui aurais pris les yeux. »
paragraphs.en: At last, Tam Lin became a man again. “Had I known what a human heart could do,” said the Queen bitterly, “I would have taken his eyes.”
paragraphs.kana: At last, Tam Lin became a man again. “Had I known what a human heart could do,” said the Queen bitterly, “I would have taken his eyes.”

paragraphs.jp: Then the fairies vanished, and Janet and Tam Lin walked home together as the sun rose.
paragraphs.fr: Puis les fées disparurent, et Janet et Tam Lin rentrèrent ensemble tandis que le soleil se levait.
paragraphs.en: Then the fairies vanished, and Janet and Tam Lin walked home together as the sun rose.
paragraphs.kana: Then the fairies vanished, and Janet and Tam Lin walked home together as the sun rose.

q.fr: Que fait la reine pour forcer Janet à lâcher Tam Lin ?
q.en: What does the Queen do to make Janet let go?

choices.fr: Elle le transforme en créatures et en fer brûlant
choices.en: She turns him into creatures and burning iron

q.fr: Que regrette la reine à la fin ?
q.en: What does the Queen regret at the end?

choices.fr: De ne pas avoir pris les yeux de Tam Lin
choices.en: Not having taken Tam Lin’s eyes

summary.fr: Le prince Llywelyn part à la chasse en laissant son fils sous la garde de son chien Gelert. À son retour, il découvre une scène terrible et agit sans réfléchir.
summary.en: Prince Llywelyn goes hunting, leaving his son in the care of his hound Gelert. On his return, he finds a terrible scene and acts without thinking.

paragraphs.jp: In the thirteenth century, Prince Llywelyn of Wales owned a hound called Gelert, which was said to be the most loyal dog in the kingdom.
paragraphs.fr: Au XIIIe siècle, le prince Llywelyn de Galles possédait un chien nommé Gelert, que l’on disait le plus fidèle du royaume.
paragraphs.en: In the thirteenth century, Prince Llywelyn of Wales owned a hound called Gelert, which was said to be the most loyal dog in the kingdom.
paragraphs.kana: In the thirteenth century, Prince Llywelyn of Wales owned a hound called Gelert, which was said to be the most loyal dog in the kingdom.

paragraphs.jp: Gelert went everywhere with the prince, and nobody could remember seeing one without the other.
paragraphs.fr: Gelert accompagnait le prince partout, et personne ne se souvenait d’avoir vu l’un sans l’autre.
paragraphs.en: Gelert went everywhere with the prince, and nobody could remember seeing one without the other.
paragraphs.kana: Gelert went everywhere with the prince, and nobody could remember seeing one without the other.

paragraphs.jp: One day, however, Llywelyn decided to go hunting without him, leaving the dog to guard his baby son.
paragraphs.fr: Un jour pourtant, Llywelyn décida d’aller chasser sans lui, laissant le chien veiller sur son bébé.
paragraphs.en: One day, however, Llywelyn decided to go hunting without him, leaving the dog to guard his baby son.
paragraphs.kana: One day, however, Llywelyn decided to go hunting without him, leaving the dog to guard his baby son.

paragraphs.jp: “Look after him,” the prince said, before riding off into the mountains of Snowdonia.
paragraphs.fr: « Veille sur lui », dit le prince avant de partir à cheval vers les montagnes de Snowdonia.
paragraphs.en: “Look after him,” the prince said, before riding off into the mountains of Snowdonia.
paragraphs.kana: “Look after him,” the prince said, before riding off into the mountains of Snowdonia.

q.en: What was said about Gelert?

choices.fr: Qu’il était le chien le plus fidèle du royaume
choices.en: That he was the most loyal dog in the kingdom

q.fr: Pourquoi Gelert ne part-il pas à la chasse ce jour-là ?
q.en: Why doesn’t Gelert go hunting that day?

paragraphs.jp: When the prince returned, Gelert ran to meet him, wagging his tail. His mouth was covered in blood.
paragraphs.fr: Quand le prince revint, Gelert courut à sa rencontre en remuant la queue. Sa gueule était couverte de sang.
paragraphs.en: When the prince returned, Gelert ran to meet him, wagging his tail. His mouth was covered in blood.
paragraphs.kana: When the prince returned, Gelert ran to meet him, wagging his tail. His mouth was covered in blood.

paragraphs.jp: Llywelyn rushed into the house: the cradle had been turned over and his son was nowhere to be seen.
paragraphs.fr: Llywelyn se précipita dans la maison : le berceau était renversé et son fils restait introuvable.
paragraphs.en: Llywelyn rushed into the house: the cradle had been turned over and his son was nowhere to be seen.
paragraphs.kana: Llywelyn rushed into the house: the cradle had been turned over and his son was nowhere to be seen.

paragraphs.jp: Convinced that the dog had killed the child, the prince drew his sword and struck Gelert, who died with a last cry.
paragraphs.fr: Convaincu que le chien avait tué l’enfant, le prince tira son épée et frappa Gelert, qui mourut en poussant un dernier cri.
paragraphs.en: Convinced that the dog had killed the child, the prince drew his sword and struck Gelert, who died with a last cry.
paragraphs.kana: Convinced that the dog had killed the child, the prince drew his sword and struck Gelert, who died with a last cry.

paragraphs.jp: At that very moment, a baby’s voice answered from under the cradle.
paragraphs.fr: À cet instant précis, la voix d’un bébé répondit sous le berceau.
paragraphs.en: At that very moment, a baby’s voice answered from under the cradle.
paragraphs.kana: At that very moment, a baby’s voice answered from under the cradle.

q.fr: Pourquoi le prince croit-il que Gelert a tué son fils ?
q.en: Why does the prince think Gelert killed his son?

choices.fr: Le chien a du sang sur la gueule et l’enfant a disparu
choices.en: The dog has blood on his mouth and the child is missing

choices.fr: Un serviteur le lui a dit

q.fr: Que se passe-t-il juste après la mort de Gelert ?
q.en: What happens just after Gelert dies?

choices.fr: On entend le bébé sous le berceau
choices.en: The baby is heard under the cradle

paragraphs.jp: Under the cradle lay the baby, unharmed, and beside him lay an enormous dead wolf.
paragraphs.fr: Sous le berceau se trouvait le bébé, indemne, et à côté de lui gisait un énorme loup mort.
paragraphs.en: Under the cradle lay the baby, unharmed, and beside him lay an enormous dead wolf.
paragraphs.kana: Under the cradle lay the baby, unharmed, and beside him lay an enormous dead wolf.

paragraphs.jp: Llywelyn understood at once: Gelert had not attacked his son but had saved him from the wolf.
paragraphs.fr: Llywelyn comprit aussitôt : Gelert n’avait pas attaqué son fils, il l’avait sauvé du loup.
paragraphs.en: Llywelyn understood at once: Gelert had not attacked his son but had saved him from the wolf.
paragraphs.kana: Llywelyn understood at once: Gelert had not attacked his son but had saved him from the wolf.

paragraphs.jp: Had he waited a moment longer, his faithful hound would still be alive. The prince was said never to have smiled again.
paragraphs.fr: S’il avait attendu un instant de plus, son fidèle chien serait encore en vie. On dit que le prince ne sourit plus jamais.
paragraphs.en: Had he waited a moment longer, his faithful hound would still be alive. The prince was said never to have smiled again.
paragraphs.kana: Had he waited a moment longer, his faithful hound would still be alive. The prince was said never to have smiled again.

paragraphs.jp: He buried Gelert with great honour, and the village of Beddgelert, which means “Gelert’s grave”, still bears his name today.
paragraphs.fr: Il enterra Gelert avec de grands honneurs, et le village de Beddgelert, qui signifie « la tombe de Gelert », porte encore son nom aujourd’hui.
paragraphs.en: He buried Gelert with great honour, and the village of Beddgelert, which means “Gelert’s grave”, still bears his name today.
paragraphs.kana: He buried Gelert with great honour, and the village of Beddgelert, which means “Gelert’s grave”, still bears his name today.

q.en: What had really happened?

choices.fr: Gelert avait sauvé le bébé d’un loup
choices.en: Gelert had saved the baby from a wolf

choices.fr: Le bébé était tombé du berceau
choices.en: The baby had fallen from the cradle

q.en: What does the name Beddgelert mean?

summary.fr: Enfermée dans une tour près de Camelot, une jeune femme ne peut regarder le monde qu’à travers un miroir. Le jour où elle voit passer Lancelot, elle brave la malédiction.
summary.en: Shut away in a tower near Camelot, a young woman may only look at the world through a mirror. The day she sees Lancelot ride by, she defies the curse.

paragraphs.jp: On an island in the river that flows down to Camelot stood a grey tower, in which lived a lady whom hardly anyone had ever seen.
paragraphs.fr: Sur une île de la rivière qui descend vers Camelot se dressait une tour grise, où vivait une dame que presque personne n’avait jamais vue.
paragraphs.en: On an island in the river that flows down to Camelot stood a grey tower, in which lived a lady whom hardly anyone had ever seen.
paragraphs.kana: On an island in the river that flows down to Camelot stood a grey tower, in which lived a lady whom hardly anyone had ever seen.

paragraphs.jp: Day and night she wove a magic tapestry, for she had been told that, were she to look directly at the outside world, a curse would fall upon her.
paragraphs.fr: Jour et nuit, elle tissait une tapisserie magique, car on lui avait dit que si elle regardait directement le monde extérieur, une malédiction s’abattrait sur elle.
paragraphs.en: Day and night she wove a magic tapestry, for she had been told that, were she to look directly at the outside world, a curse would fall upon her.
paragraphs.kana: Day and night she wove a magic tapestry, for she had been told that, were she to look directly at the outside world, a curse would fall upon her.

paragraphs.jp: Not knowing what the curse might be, she dared not disobey, and watched life pass only as reflections in a mirror.
paragraphs.fr: Ignorant la nature de cette malédiction, elle n’osait désobéir et ne voyait passer la vie que sous forme de reflets dans un miroir.
paragraphs.en: Not knowing what the curse might be, she dared not disobey, and watched life pass only as reflections in a mirror.
paragraphs.kana: Not knowing what the curse might be, she dared not disobey, and watched life pass only as reflections in a mirror.

paragraphs.jp: Farmers, knights and young lovers appeared in the glass, yet she remained, in her own words, “half sick of shadows”.
paragraphs.fr: Paysans, chevaliers et jeunes amoureux apparaissaient dans la glace ; pourtant, elle restait, selon ses propres mots, « à demi lasse des ombres ».
paragraphs.en: Farmers, knights and young lovers appeared in the glass, yet she remained, in her own words, “half sick of shadows”.
paragraphs.kana: Farmers, knights and young lovers appeared in the glass, yet she remained, in her own words, “half sick of shadows”.

q.fr: Que se passerait-il si la dame regardait directement dehors ?
q.en: What would happen if the lady looked directly outside?

choices.en: A curse would fall upon her

q.en: How does she see the world?

paragraphs.jp: One bright summer morning, Sir Lancelot rode past the tower, his armour flashing in the sun and his voice ringing out in song.
paragraphs.fr: Un lumineux matin d’été, sire Lancelot passa près de la tour, son armure étincelant au soleil et sa voix résonnant dans une chanson.
paragraphs.en: One bright summer morning, Sir Lancelot rode past the tower, his armour flashing in the sun and his voice ringing out in song.
paragraphs.kana: One bright summer morning, Sir Lancelot rode past the tower, his armour flashing in the sun and his voice ringing out in song.

paragraphs.jp: No sooner had his reflection crossed the mirror than the lady left her loom and went to the window.
paragraphs.fr: À peine son reflet eut-il traversé le miroir que la dame quitta son métier à tisser et alla à la fenêtre.
paragraphs.en: No sooner had his reflection crossed the mirror than the lady left her loom and went to the window.
paragraphs.kana: No sooner had his reflection crossed the mirror than the lady left her loom and went to the window.

paragraphs.jp: At that very moment, the mirror cracked from side to side and the tapestry flew out of the window.
paragraphs.fr: À cet instant précis, le miroir se fendit d’un bout à l’autre et la tapisserie s’envola par la fenêtre.
paragraphs.en: At that very moment, the mirror cracked from side to side and the tapestry flew out of the window.
paragraphs.kana: At that very moment, the mirror cracked from side to side and the tapestry flew out of the window.

paragraphs.jp: “The curse is come upon me,” she cried, knowing that there was no turning back.
paragraphs.fr: « La malédiction s’abat sur moi », s’écria-t-elle, sachant qu’il n’y avait plus de retour possible.
paragraphs.en: “The curse is come upon me,” she cried, knowing that there was no turning back.
paragraphs.kana: “The curse is come upon me,” she cried, knowing that there was no turning back.

q.fr: Qu’est-ce qui pousse la dame à aller à la fenêtre ?
q.en: What makes the lady go to the window?

q.fr: Que se passe-t-il quand elle regarde dehors ?
q.en: What happens when she looks outside?

paragraphs.jp: Sensing that her end was near, she found a boat beneath a willow, wrote her name upon its prow and lay down in it.
paragraphs.fr: Pressentant sa fin proche, elle trouva une barque sous un saule, inscrivit son nom sur la proue et s’y allongea.
paragraphs.en: Sensing that her end was near, she found a boat beneath a willow, wrote her name upon its prow and lay down in it.
paragraphs.kana: Sensing that her end was near, she found a boat beneath a willow, wrote her name upon its prow and lay down in it.

paragraphs.jp: The boat drifted down the river towards Camelot as she sang her last song, her voice growing ever fainter.
paragraphs.fr: La barque dériva sur la rivière vers Camelot tandis qu’elle chantait son dernier chant, d’une voix de plus en plus faible.
paragraphs.en: The boat drifted down the river towards Camelot as she sang her last song, her voice growing ever fainter.
paragraphs.kana: The boat drifted down the river towards Camelot as she sang her last song, her voice growing ever fainter.

paragraphs.jp: By the time it reached the town, she had died. Knights and ladies gathered on the bank, wondering who she might have been.
paragraphs.fr: Le temps qu’elle atteigne la ville, la dame était morte. Chevaliers et dames se rassemblèrent sur la rive, se demandant qui elle avait bien pu être.
paragraphs.en: By the time it reached the town, she had died. Knights and ladies gathered on the bank, wondering who she might have been.
paragraphs.kana: By the time it reached the town, she had died. Knights and ladies gathered on the bank, wondering who she might have been.

paragraphs.jp: Only Lancelot paused to look at her face, and, unaware of the part he had played, said simply that she had a lovely face.
paragraphs.fr: Seul Lancelot s’arrêta pour regarder son visage et, ignorant le rôle qu’il avait joué, dit simplement qu’elle avait un beau visage.
paragraphs.en: Only Lancelot paused to look at her face, and, unaware of the part he had played, said simply that she had a lovely face.
paragraphs.kana: Only Lancelot paused to look at her face, and, unaware of the part he had played, said simply that she had a lovely face.

q.fr: Qu’écrit la dame sur la barque ?
q.en: What does the lady write on the boat?

q.fr: Que sait Lancelot de son rôle dans l’histoire ?
q.en: What does Lancelot know about his part in the story?

summary.fr: Le poète écossais Thomas d’Erceldoune rencontre la reine d’Elfland sous un arbre. Il la suit dans son royaume, où le temps ne s’écoule pas comme ailleurs.
summary.en: The Scottish poet Thomas of Erceldoune meets the Queen of Elfland beneath a tree. He follows her into her kingdom, where time does not pass as it does elsewhere.

paragraphs.jp: Thomas of Erceldoune, a poet renowned throughout the Borders, was resting beneath the Eildon Tree when a lady of dazzling beauty rode towards him.
paragraphs.fr: Thomas d’Erceldoune, poète renommé dans tous les Borders, se reposait sous l’arbre d’Eildon quand une dame d’une beauté éblouissante s’avança vers lui à cheval.
paragraphs.en: Thomas of Erceldoune, a poet renowned throughout the Borders, was resting beneath the Eildon Tree when a lady of dazzling beauty rode towards him.
paragraphs.kana: Thomas of Erceldoune, a poet renowned throughout the Borders, was resting beneath the Eildon Tree when a lady of dazzling beauty rode towards him.

paragraphs.jp: Her horse was white as milk, and from its mane hung fifty silver bells that rang with every step.
paragraphs.fr: Son cheval était blanc comme le lait, et à sa crinière pendaient cinquante clochettes d’argent qui tintaient à chaque pas.
paragraphs.en: Her horse was white as milk, and from its mane hung fifty silver bells that rang with every step.
paragraphs.kana: Her horse was white as milk, and from its mane hung fifty silver bells that rang with every step.

paragraphs.jp: Mistaking her for the Queen of Heaven, Thomas knelt before her, only to be told that she was the Queen of fair Elfland.
paragraphs.fr: La prenant pour la Reine des Cieux, Thomas s’agenouilla devant elle, avant d’apprendre qu’elle était la reine de la belle Elfland.
paragraphs.en: Mistaking her for the Queen of Heaven, Thomas knelt before her, only to be told that she was the Queen of fair Elfland.
paragraphs.kana: Mistaking her for the Queen of Heaven, Thomas knelt before her, only to be told that she was the Queen of fair Elfland.

paragraphs.jp: Bold, albeit unwise, he kissed her, thereby binding himself to serve her for seven years.
paragraphs.fr: Audacieux, bien qu’imprudent, il l’embrassa, se liant ainsi à elle pour la servir sept ans.
paragraphs.en: Bold, albeit unwise, he kissed her, thereby binding himself to serve her for seven years.
paragraphs.kana: Bold, albeit unwise, he kissed her, thereby binding himself to serve her for seven years.

q.fr: Pour qui Thomas prend-il d’abord la dame ?
q.en: Who does Thomas first take the lady to be?

q.fr: Quelle est la conséquence du baiser ?
q.en: What is the consequence of the kiss?

choices.fr: Il doit la servir sept ans
choices.en: He must serve her for seven years

paragraphs.jp: They rode for forty days through darkness, wading through rivers of blood, until they came to a place where three roads met.
paragraphs.fr: Ils chevauchèrent quarante jours dans l’obscurité, traversant à gué des rivières de sang, jusqu’à un lieu où trois chemins se rejoignaient.
paragraphs.en: They rode for forty days through darkness, wading through rivers of blood, until they came to a place where three roads met.
paragraphs.kana: They rode for forty days through darkness, wading through rivers of blood, until they came to a place where three roads met.

paragraphs.jp: The first, narrow and thorny, was the path of righteousness; the second, broad and easy, led to wickedness.
paragraphs.fr: Le premier, étroit et épineux, était le chemin de la vertu ; le second, large et facile, menait au vice.
paragraphs.en: The first, narrow and thorny, was the path of righteousness; the second, broad and easy, led to wickedness.
paragraphs.kana: The first, narrow and thorny, was the path of righteousness; the second, broad and easy, led to wickedness.

paragraphs.jp: The third, winding up a hillside of ferns, was the road to fair Elfland, and it was this one that they took.
paragraphs.fr: Le troisième, serpentant sur un coteau de fougères, était la route de la belle Elfland, et c’est celui qu’ils prirent.
paragraphs.en: The third, winding up a hillside of ferns, was the road to fair Elfland, and it was this one that they took.
paragraphs.kana: The third, winding up a hillside of ferns, was the road to fair Elfland, and it was this one that they took.

paragraphs.jp: “Should you speak a single word while you are in my land,” the Queen warned, “you will never return to your own.”
paragraphs.fr: « Si tu prononces un seul mot pendant ton séjour dans mon royaume, avertit la reine, tu ne reverras jamais le tien. »
paragraphs.en: “Should you speak a single word while you are in my land,” the Queen warned, “you will never return to your own.”
paragraphs.kana: “Should you speak a single word while you are in my land,” the Queen warned, “you will never return to your own.”

q.en: Which road leads to Elfland?

choices.fr: Le chemin sinueux parmi les fougères
choices.en: The winding road among the ferns

q.fr: Que ne doit pas faire Thomas à Elfland ?
q.en: What must Thomas not do in Elfland?

paragraphs.jp: Thomas kept silent for what seemed to him three days, only to discover that seven years had passed.
paragraphs.fr: Thomas garda le silence pendant ce qui lui sembla trois jours, avant de découvrir que sept années s’étaient écoulées.
paragraphs.en: Thomas kept silent for what seemed to him three days, only to discover that seven years had passed.
paragraphs.kana: Thomas kept silent for what seemed to him three days, only to discover that seven years had passed.

paragraphs.jp: Before sending him home, the Queen gave him a tongue that could never lie, a gift he considered, to some extent, a burden.
paragraphs.fr: Avant de le renvoyer chez lui, la reine lui donna une langue incapable de mentir, un don qu’il considéra, dans une certaine mesure, comme un fardeau.
paragraphs.en: Before sending him home, the Queen gave him a tongue that could never lie, a gift he considered, to some extent, a burden.
paragraphs.kana: Before sending him home, the Queen gave him a tongue that could never lie, a gift he considered, to some extent, a burden.

paragraphs.jp: Back in Scotland, he became famous for his prophecies, many of which were said to have come true.
paragraphs.fr: De retour en Écosse, il devint célèbre pour ses prophéties, dont beaucoup se seraient réalisées.
paragraphs.en: Back in Scotland, he became famous for his prophecies, many of which were said to have come true.
paragraphs.kana: Back in Scotland, he became famous for his prophecies, many of which were said to have come true.

paragraphs.jp: Years later, when two white deer appeared at his door, he followed them into the forest and was never seen again.
paragraphs.fr: Des années plus tard, quand deux cerfs blancs apparurent à sa porte, il les suivit dans la forêt et on ne le revit jamais.
paragraphs.en: Years later, when two white deer appeared at his door, he followed them into the forest and was never seen again.
paragraphs.kana: Years later, when two white deer appeared at his door, he followed them into the forest and was never seen again.

q.fr: Combien de temps Thomas est-il vraiment resté à Elfland ?
q.en: How long did Thomas really stay in Elfland?

q.fr: Quel don reçoit-il de la reine ?
q.en: What gift does he receive from the Queen?

choices.fr: Une langue qui ne peut mentir

title.fr: Les trois déménagements de la mère de Mencius
